children.name: Hemiprocne
children.description: Elegant, long-winged swifts with a distinctive crest and a forked tail, differing from true swifts in their habit of perching conspicuously in trees. They are among the most graceful aerialists of the Asian and Australasian tropics.

children.name: Hemiprocne coronata
children.description: The crested treeswift (Hemiprocne coronata) is a species of tree swift.

children.name: Hemiprocne mystacea
children.description: The moustached treeswift (Hemiprocne mystacea) is a species of bird in the family Hemiprocnidae.

children.name: Hemiprocne longipennis
children.description: The grey-rumped treeswift (Hemiprocne longipennis) is a species of bird in the Hemiprocnidae family. Currently, four extant species are placed in the family. Like the other members of the Hemiprocnidae, this species is closely related to true swifts, but unlike true swifts, the treeswifts are arboreal, often seen perched on trees, high-tension power transmission lines, and pylons. When perched, the wing tips cross over the tail. This species is commonly found in peninsular Malaysia, but has an extremely large range; there is limited information about population trends.

children.name: Hemiprocne bartletti
children.description: A medium-sized treeswift endemic to the Santa Cruz Islands of the Solomon Archipelago. It has glossy blue-black upperparts, a white belly, and a deeply forked tail. The male has a chestnut face and throat while the female has a dark face. It hunts insects in high-speed aerial forays above lowland forests and coconut plantations.
